classification.difficultyReason: The student must choose the largest and smallest angles unprompted, apply the cosine rule twice, then subtract. This is slightly more than the signposted reference.

content.prompt: Find the difference between the largest and smallest angles of this triangle, to 1 decimal place.

answer.worked:
The largest angle $L$ is opposite $11\text{ m}$ and the smallest angle $S$ is opposite $6\text{ m}$.
$$\begin{align*}\cos L&=\frac{6^2+9^2-11^2}{2(6)(9)}\\[8pt]L&=\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{27}\right)\approx92.12^\circ\\[8pt]\cos S&=\frac{9^2+11^2-6^2}{2(9)(11)}\\[8pt]S&=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{83}{99}\right)\approx33.03^\circ\\[8pt]L-S&\approx59.1^\circ\end{align*}$$
